question.problem:
Simplify the statement $
eg ( (P \lor 
eg Q) \land (Q \lor 
eg P) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q, \\ ¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((P∨¬Q)∧(Q∨¬P)) & ≡¬(P∨¬Q)∨¬(Q∨¬P) \\  & ≡(¬P∧¬(¬Q))∨(¬Q∧¬(¬P)) \\  & ≡(¬P∧Q)∨(¬Q∧P)\end{aligned}
$$
